articles.title: Patrick Mahomes desperately needs help, but Tyreek Hill may no longer be the answer for Chiefs
articles.standfirst: Kansas City is running out of solutions, but bringing back a familiar face may not be the move the team needs right now
articles.summary: Kansas City is running out of solutions, but bringing back a familiar face may not be the move the team needs right now
articles.body:
The season continues to move forward, and the paths of the Kansas City Chiefs and Tyreek Hill appear to be heading in opposite directions . Patrick Mahomes and the team are going through a difficult stretch, putting Hill back in the conversation as a potential asset who could help them turn things around .

After the loss to the Denver Broncos, Mahomes acknowledged that miscommunication between him, the receivers and the running backs had affected the team's execution . His comments reopened discussions about Hill, a former Chiefs star who remains available and has expressed interest in returning to football.

However, a reunion may not be the right move at this point. Kansas City cannot afford more mistakes if it wants to get back on the winning track, while Hill is coming off an injury that ended his season and effectively closed his chapter with the Miami Dolphins . The team has since moved toward younger options, including three drafted rookies: Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman Jr., alongside Malik Washington, who is still developing.

The Chiefs already have options at receiver

Kansas City's situation is not entirely different. The Chiefs have players who are expected to make an impact, but they have not consistently performed at their potential. Rashee Rice was selected in the second round, while Xavier Worthy was a first-round pick. Players with that kind of draft investment are supposed to be part of the solution.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ “I have to be a dad too” quote resurfaces as the Chiefs look to bounce back
articles.standfirst: The quarterback’s reflections on family feel timely as Kansas City tries to recover from back-to-back losses
articles.summary: The quarterback’s reflections on family feel timely as Kansas City tries to recover from back-to-back losses
articles.body:
“Everybody sees the game days,” Patrick Mahomes said in Netflix’s Quarterback. What fans don’t see, he explained, is the day-to-day work of balancing football with life as a father and husband. “I have to be a dad too. I have to be a husband.” The comments have resurfaced as the Kansas City Chiefs look to steady their season.

They are not from a new interview. But they offer a personal glimpse of the life he shares with his wife, Brittany, and their three children, Sterling, Bronze and Golden , beyond the pressure of Sundays and the chase for another Super Bowl.

Family life beyond the Chiefs’ latest losses

The timing gives Mahomes’ words new resonance. Kansas City opened the season 5-0 , then lost 20-3 to the Seattle Seahawks and 28-24 to the Denver Broncos in consecutive weeks.

The loss in Denver was especially painful: the Chiefs led by 11 in the fourth quarter and reached the Broncos’ 1-yard line late, but came away without the go-ahead score.

After the Denver game, Mahomes didn’t hide from the stakes. “Now, you’re kind of in a dogfight for the division,” he said, adding that the team had to take it one week at a time.

For a quarterback carrying the hopes of a franchise, those words show the weight of the job; his earlier comments also remind fans that football is only one part of his life.

The Chiefs’ next chance to respond comes Sunday, Nov. 8, at home against the New York Jets . Kickoff is at noon CT (1 p.m. ET) on CBS and Paramount+.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark backs the Chiefs for the Super Bowl and surprises by choosing between Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes
articles.standfirst: The WNBA star spoke about Kansas City's season and made it clear who ranks first among her favorite players. Her answer put Travis Kelce ahead of quarterback Patrick Mahomes.
articles.summary: The WNBA star spoke about Kansas City's season and made it clear who ranks first among her favorite players. Her answer put Travis Kelce ahead of quarterback Patrick Mahomes.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark doesn't lose sight of the Kansas City Chiefs. Although her career is tied to basketball and the Indiana Fever, the WNBA star closely follows the NFL team and has more than enough reasons to feel excited about its present. In a recent conversation, she shared her thoughts on the season and left a remark that caught the attention of fans.

But the most talked-about moment came when she was asked about her favorite players in the franchise. Clark did not hesitate: she chose Travis Kelce over Patrick Mahomes , an answer that surprised some Kansas City fans because of the importance the quarterback has on the team.

Caitlin Clark explained why she trusts the Chiefs

The basketball player spoke about the team's recovery after a previous campaign marked by injuries. Although she acknowledged that the game against the Seattle Seahawks had not been good for Kansas City, she also highlighted the opponent's level and was optimistic about what lies ahead.

It's like they make everything look really easy. Obviously, the game against the Seahawks the other week wasn't good for us, but that's okay. Seattle is a good team, but it's been fun to see how they've managed to bounce back this year. Last year was complicated because of the injuries and everything else, but this year I have a good feeling

The statement about her favorites came when Kylie Kelce asked her whether Travis was her favorite Chiefs player of all time. The response was emphatic and also included recognition of another Kansas City legend.

Of course he is! I was also a fan of Tony Gonzalez when I was little, but no. Travis is definitely my favorite Chiefs player of all time, and Patrick is right behind him. It’s been so much fun following them

The player grew up in Des Moines, Iowa, and previously explained that her father was a Chiefs fan and that the franchise was the NFL team closest to her city.

In an appearance on Travis and Jason Kelce's New Heights podcast, she said she had already been following the team before Mahomes and Kelce arrived. "People think I'm a Chiefs fan because it's trendy, but I was already there before Patrick and Travis," she explained at the time.

Thus, Clark once again showed that her support for Kansas City goes beyond a visit to the stadium or an appearance alongside Taylor Swift. Her confidence in the team's recovery and her choice of Kelce over Mahomes offered yet another sign of a fandom that has been with her since childhood.

articles.title: Travis Kelce disappears from Chiefs locker room and returns in a condition that raises eyebrows after brutal loss
articles.standfirst: The Kansas City Chiefs have shown major flaws since starting the 2026 season with a 5-0 record.
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have shown major flaws since starting the 2026 season with a 5-0 record.
articles.body:
While two losses shouldn't be considered a catastrophe, it's safe to say that the Kansas City Chiefs are in the midst of a slide. After a 5-0 start, everything seemed fine and dandy, but there were real issues festering underneath the undefeated record.

Their first loss to the Seattle Seahawks was concerning, but somewhat expected against the reigning Super Bowl champions on the road. The week after against the Denver Broncos actually featured a Chiefs team playing much better, but poor in-game decisions from Andy Reid and an overall team collapse in the fourth quarter left the team in a sensitive emotional state.

Travis Kelce had to gather himself, emotionally, before addressing media after Broncos loss

Travis Kelce was the picture boy in that regard. Following the game, Kelce spoke with reporters in the Chiefs locker room, but before he did he had to gather himself by " heading around a corner and briefly disappearing " before coming back. Then, when he spoke with the media, his eyes were red and he was visibly emotional .

Kelce really beat himself up for the loss to the Broncos. He believes he let his team down, even though he had a solid performance with five catches for 67 yards .

The reality of things is that we've got to fix a lot. The little things, mistakes. And it starts with the person that you're looking at in the mirror. I'm one of them. I've been frustrated with myself on how long I've been in the league, and the procedural stuff that's happened, for the past three games really... You just can't f***ing do it. I gotta be better for my teammates. And that sets the tone for a lot of people in this room. Everybody's just gotta up the ante from that.

The two losses have clearly affected Kelce from a mental and emotional standpoint. Given that this is likely his final season in the NFL, he wants to go out with a Super Bowl . But in order for that to happen, he and the Chiefs have to be perfect in every facet of play . That simply isn't happening right now.

articles.title: Brittany Mahomes responds to haters with unexpected message after complaining about officiating against the Chiefs: “I pray that God…”
articles.standfirst: Patrick Mahomes' wife has turned her attention to faith and family after criticizing a controversial penalty that cost Kansas City a potential victory
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes' wife has turned her attention to faith and family after criticizing a controversial penalty that cost Kansas City a potential victory
articles.body:
Brittany Mahomes has never been afraid to defend her husband or the Kansas City Chiefs , but her latest social media activity has revealed a different side of the emotions surrounding the team's difficult start to November.

The wife of quarterback Patrick Mahomes recently criticized NFL officials following Kansas City's controversial 28-24 defeat against the Denver Broncos , a result that left the franchise dealing with consecutive losses and mounting questions about its performances.

However, Brittany subsequently shared a religious message with her followers, emphasizing hope and peace during a period when the Chiefs have been facing increasing scrutiny.

Brittany wrote: "Not sure who needs to hear this today, but... I pray that God, the source of hope, will fill you completely with joy and peace because you trust in him. Then you will overflow with confident hope through the power of the Holy Spirit. Romans 15:13."

The post arrived shortly after her outspoken reaction to the Broncos game. Her message was accompanied by another personal reflection, this time celebrating motherhood and the happiness she finds in raising her three children with Patrick.

Brittany shares emotional message after Chiefs defeat

Brittany 's latest posts represented a noticeable change in tone after she expressed frustration with the officials who penalized Kansas City during the closing moments against Denver.

The Chiefs appeared to have secured a dramatic victory when Mahomes found Rashee Rice in the end zone, only for a false start penalty against offensive tackle Jaylon Moore to erase the touchdown.

Following the decision, Brittany criticized the officials on Instagram, describing it as "the weakest call I have ever seen" and questioning why the penalty had been called.

Her subsequent family-focused message offered a different perspective on what matters most to her outside the NFL.

"Sometimes I just look at my kids and think, how did I get so lucky that I actually made my favorite people in the entire world?" she wrote. "Like, I grew these little humans and now I get to spend my life loving them. Nothing will ever beat that."

Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid under pressure

While Brittany has focused on family and faith, Patrick and the Chiefs must address the mistakes that contributed to their latest defeat.

Kansas City surrendered an 11-point advantage in the fourth quarter, with Denver scoring 15 unanswered points before the disputed penalty ended the Chiefs ' final opportunity.

Mahomes finished with 321 passing yards and three touchdowns, but Kansas City's 11 penalties for 105 yards proved particularly damaging.

Chiefs coach Andy Reid acknowledged that discipline had become a significant concern following the loss.

"Offensively, it really came down to that. You win the game if you don't have the penalty on the score there at the end, with very little time left on the clock," Reid explained.

With Kansas City attempting to recover from consecutive defeats, Brittany 's latest reflections have provided a contrast to the frustration surrounding the team.

Rather than extending her criticism of the officials, she has chosen to share messages centered on gratitude, motherhood and faith.

articles.title: Chiefs backed into a corner to pursue one big-name receiver for Patrick Mahomes
articles.standfirst: Kansas City may have found a more realistic trade target who could address its immediate needs
articles.summary: Kansas City may have found a more realistic trade target who could address its immediate needs
articles.body:
T hings are starting to shake up in Kansas City after a series of disappointing results forced the Chiefs to acknowledge that several areas need immediate improvement. The team still has time to turn things around, but finding the right addition before the NFL trade deadline could help Andy Reid get his offense back on track.

The conversation surrounding Tyreek Hill is gradually losing momentum. Although the wide receiver has been mentioned as a potential target, he might not be the solution Kansas City desperately need s. Another option is starting to look more appealing, especially because his playing style could fit Reid's offensive approach.

Josh Downs could be the answer for Kansas City

Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs could check several of the boxes the Chiefs are looking for, particularly after reportedly requesting a trade from his current team. The potential move could benefit both sides, as Kansas City needs another reliable target for Patrick Mahomes, while Downs could use a quarterback who gives him a better opportunity to showcase his abilities.

The fourth-year receiver could look considerably more productive in an offense with a functional quarterback consistently getting him the football. That is where Mahomes could make a difference, giving Downs an opportunity to become a more important part of the passing game.

A move that could solve more than one problem

The biggest advantage of pursuing Downs is that Kansas City would not necessarily be making a short-term move just to get through the season. Unlike a veteran approaching the final stages of his career, Downs is a fourth-year player who could become a long-term piece of the Chiefs' wide receiver room.

There are also concerns about the team's current core getting older, with some of its most important players continuing to carry much of the responsibility. Travis Kelce is among those whose time in Kansas City could become more limited, making it increasingly important for the Chiefs to establish stability at the position before they are forced to find replacements.

Kansas City has relied on Kelce as one of Mahomes' most dependable options for years. However, the team will eventually need more established pass catchers to take on some of that responsibility. Building that foundation now would be a smarter approach than waiting until the need becomes more urgent.

The Chiefs cannot afford to wait

The Chiefs need long-term answers at wide receiver, and Downs could be a viable addition with the potential to provide even more value if the team decided to negotiate an early contract extension . His age and potential make him an option worth considering beyond the immediate needs of the season.

Still, some could see the move as a potential risk. But if Downs is not the right choice, does that automatically make Hill a better option? Kansas City cannot assume that other teams are overlooking what the Colts receiver could bring to the table. If the Chiefs hesitate, another contender chasing a Lombardi Trophy this season could recognize the same opportunity and make its move first. Mahomes needs receivers who can consistently turn his passes into plays, and Downs could offer a more practical solution for an offense searching for answers . The Chiefs have to decide whether he is the right investment before someone else gets the chance to bring him in.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes pulled off a perfect deal by selling his mansion in Kansas City for $2.9 million and finding a buyer in record time
articles.standfirst: Mahomes has sold the first home he ever purchased after his breakout 2018 NFL season
articles.summary: Mahomes has sold the first home he ever purchased after his breakout 2018 NFL season
articles.body:
P atrick Mahomes has enjoyed plenty of memorable victories during his career, but one of his earliest investments away from football also proved successful as the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback secured an impressive return on his first home after selling the property. The mansion sold for an asking price of $2.9 million despite the fact that Mahomes originally purchased the Kansas City residence for $1.9 million in February 2019, shortly after collecting the NFL MVP award following his breakout 2018 season.

Four years later, the property attracted a buyer in less than two weeks after hitting the market. Located at 1257 W. 57th St. in the prestigious Sunset Hill neighborhood, the ranch-style property was built in 1953 and occupied approximately 1.4 acres. It represented an important milestone for Mahomes and his then-girlfriend Brittany Matthews , who would later become his wife as the couple invested nearly $400,000 renovating the residence, transforming it into a luxurious family home as he established himself among the NFL elite. He previously described it as the first house either of them had owned, making the purchase particularly significant whilst the finished property featured an open-plan layout and several personalized additions, including a dedicated sneaker room reportedly capable of holding approximately 180 pairs. Outside, residents could enjoy a heated swimming pool, hot tub and putting green and a five-car garage provided additional space for the quarterback's vehicles, while the extensive grounds offered considerably more privacy than a typical residential property. However, as Mahomes ' career and family grew, the original home eventually became too small for their changing lifestyle.

Mahomes finds a buyer in less than two weeks after listing his mansion

In June 2023, Mahomes and Matthews decided to put the property on the market for $2.9 million whilst Cami Jones of ReeceNichols handled the listing, and the property was quickly snapped up. A trust connected to a local businessman named David "Rall" Bradley III purchased the residence in less than two weeks – happy to pay the asking price that represented a $1 million increase on the quarterback's original purchase price, highlighting the property's appreciation during his time there. Mahomes had already begun expanding his real estate portfolio before broadening beyond Kansas City and in March 2020, he purchased a $3.37 million property in Westlake, Texas , before his family eventually moved into a significantly larger estate in Cass County, Missouri , in 2023. Away from real estate, Mahomes faces a considerably more difficult challenge as Kansas City attempts to recover from consecutive defeats against the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos . Injuries to Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton have contributed to the team's offensive problems and ESPN's Dan Graziano reported that the Chiefs and Pittsburgh Steelers are both interested in the Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs . The 24-year-old has reportedly requested a trade following Indianapolis ' decisions to move Quenton Nelson to Seattle and DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers . Downs has recorded 30 receptions for 330 yards and one touchdown this season, having surpassed 500 receiving yards in each of his first three NFL campaigns, and two of those seasons produced more than 700 yards. Indianapolis is reportedly seeking a third-round pick, although ESPN's Adam Schefter believes that valuation could fall to a fourth-round selection as the November 10 trade deadline approaches.

Away from real estate, Mahomes faces a considerably more difficult challenge as Kansas City attempts to recover from consecutive defeats against the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos . Injuries to Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton have contributed to the team's offensive problems and ESPN's Dan Graziano reported that the Chiefs and Pittsburgh Steelers are both interested in the Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs . The 24-year-old has reportedly requested a trade following Indianapolis ' decisions to move Quenton Nelson to Seattle and DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers . Downs has recorded 30 receptions for 330 yards and one touchdown this season, having surpassed 500 receiving yards in each of his first three NFL campaigns, and two of those seasons produced more than 700 yards. Indianapolis is reportedly seeking a third-round pick, although ESPN's Adam Schefter believes that valuation could fall to a fourth-round selection as the November 10 trade deadline approaches.

articles.title: Former Chiefs player suggests Andy Reid sign George Pickens amid the Cowboys' hesitation – and Tyreek Hill won't agree
articles.standfirst: Hill remains an unsigned free agent but has been strongly linked to Kansas City
articles.summary: Hill remains an unsigned free agent but has been strongly linked to Kansas City
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs could have an opportunity to address its struggling receiving corps, with Tyrann Mathieu identifying the Dallas Cowboys ’ George Pickens as a potential game-changing addition for Patrick Mahomes . The Chiefs have been searching for answers to their offensive struggles, and the team's former safety believes the solution could be found in Dallas , where Pickens ' long-term future with the Cowboys uncertain.

Dallas committed $27.3 million to the receiver through the franchise tag for the 2026 season, but that has not settled questions about his future beyond the current campaign. And with negotiations yet to provide long-term certainty, the possibility of a trade has become an increasingly interesting storyline, prompting Mathieu to urge Andy Reid to pursue the talented player. “If I’m the Chiefs, I want to go get somebody like George Pickens. I need somebody with that kind of catch radius,” Mathieu said on his podcast. “And then like those 50-50 balls, like them one-on-one chances. “Like, we don’t see Mahomes like take a lot of those throws because he don’t have nobody to throw it to. You know what I’m saying? And so now if he got somebody that could win those plays, you know what I’m saying, 40-50 yards down the field. “Like that instantly makes him like rise - not even from like a statistical perspective, like they need some swagger. Since Tyreek Hill left, they don’t really have a swagger. Like they don’t got no identity, right? “You know what I’m saying? Like, and I think when you have somebody like George Pickens, like and that you’re gonna have to throw him the ball.”

Chiefs' receiving problems make Pickens an attractive target

Pickens would represent a significant acquisition for Kansas City after recording 1429 yards on 93 catches and nine touchdowns during the 2025 NFL season , despite competing with CeeDee Lamb for snaps. Mathieu 's argument also extends beyond statistics, with the former safety believing Kansas City has lost its offensive identity since trading Tyreek Hill to the Miami Dolphins in 2022. The Chiefs ' numbers support those concerns, ranking 27th in receptions, 30th in receiving yards and 31st in percentage of team receiving production. Their most reliable target remains 37-year-old tight end Travis Kelce . Opponents have also increasingly challenged Mahomes through the air, with the Seattle Seahawks and Broncos stacking the box and limiting Kansas City 's running game and putting the quarterback under extended pressure. Pickens is not the only potential target, with Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs and Jacksonville Jaguars wideout Brian Thomas Jr. also linked. However, Hill remains the most intriguing possibility. Kansas City reportedly contacted his agent, Drew Rosenhaus , in October to explore a reunion as Hill spent six seasons with the Chiefs between 2016 and 2021, earning six Pro Bowl selections and three All-Pro honors. After helping the franchise win Super Bowl LIV, Kansas City later t raded him following unsuccessful contract negotiations, but the Dolphins released Hill in February 2026, but his return has been complicated by a serious knee injury. He remains a free agent.

articles.title: Backtracking: Andy Reid admits defeat with quick fix to Chiefs' offensive line
articles.standfirst: Kansas City's head coach appears ready to restore Kingsley Suamataia to the starting lineup
articles.summary: Kansas City's head coach appears ready to restore Kingsley Suamataia to the starting lineup
articles.body:
Andy Reid appears ready to reverse one of his recent offensive line decisions as the Kansas City Chiefs attempt to stop their losing streak as after benching Kingsley Suamataia against the Denver Broncos , he has indicated that the guard could return to the starting lineup in Week 9.

Kansas City has lost two consecutive games after opening the season with five straight victories as its latest defeat came against divisional rival Denver , where problems protecting Patrick Mahomes contributed to a disappointing finish as the quarterback was sacked on the final play of the game.

Fans were shocked though ahead of kickoff as Suamataia was replaced by Mike Caliendo , but fortunately for the Chiefs Kingdom , the change could prove short-lived as Matt McMullen believes Reid is ready to give him a third chance in the 2026 NFL campaign.

“Coach Reid says ‘there’s a good chance' Kingsley Suamataia is back at left guard this week,” McMullen posted and the decision would restore the player who started the first three games of the season at the position.

Suamataia also started all 17 games for Kansas City last year, making his repeated appearances on the bench particularly notable and the situation has attracted attention because this is not the first time it’s happened: The young guard was previously benched against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4.

On both occasions, Reid has repeatedly declined to explain why Suamataia was removed from the lineup as he keeps his cards close to his chest but it is not injury related as Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reported the organization described that earlier decision as a "coaching decision."

Reid then offered little additional information, insisting the matter would remain between him and the player and the decision was particularly surprising given Suamataia 's performances before his first benching.

Next Gen Stats showed that he had allowed pressure on just 3.8% of his blocking opportunities entering Week 4, the lowest rate among starting left guards whilst Caliendo 's opportunity has not produced a convincing case for keeping the change permanent.

The Chiefs receive health updates ahead of Jets clash

Mahomes was sacked twice and took eight quarterback hits during the Raiders game, while Kansas City 's offensive line also struggled against Denver and the defeat to their AFC West rivals has seen the Chiefs lose control of the division, vital for seeding in the NFL Playoffs .

Should Suamataia return to the starting line up to partner center Creed Humphrey and left tackle Kahlil Benson in protecting Mahomes remains to be seen, but Reid also provided several updates on the team's availability as Kansas City prepares to host the New York Jets .

The team’s first-round pick Peter Woods was the only player unable to practice, with the defensive lineman recovering from a neck stinger meanwhile, cornerback Mansoor Delane returned to practice after missing the Denver game with a shoulder issue, providing an encouraging development for the defense.

Leading wide receiver Rashee Rice also made his return against the Broncos after missing time with a hamstring injury as he played 17 snaps in the third quarter before gradually taking on more responsibility in Week 8.

Reid also confirmed that Harrison Butker would remain the starting kicker despite another missed field goal in Denver. Kansas City recently added Justin Tucker to its practice squad, but Butker appears set to retain his role against the Jets .

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes drops ultimatum on Reid over banned play
articles.standfirst: The Chiefs quarterback revealed whether he would be willing to use the controversial short-yardage play that Andy Reid has avoided since 2019.
articles.summary: The Chiefs quarterback revealed whether he would be willing to use the controversial short-yardage play that Andy Reid has avoided since 2019.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs let a seemingly comfortable lead slip away against the Denver Broncos in Week 8 of the NFL season.

Kansas City entered the fourth quarter with a 24-13 advantage but failed to hold on, ultimately falling 28-24. The Chiefs had multiple opportunities to put the game away while leading and even had one final offensive possession to complete a comeback after surrendering the lead.

Patrick Mahomes opens the door to using QB sneaks

One of the most criticized decisions by Andy Reid in recent years has been his reluctance to use the QB sneak, a short-yardage play that many NFL teams regularly rely on in goal-line situations.

The coach’s stance dates back to 2019 , when Patrick Mahomes suffered a right kneecap injury while attempting a similar play. While many believe that incident was an unfortunate and isolated situation, fans have continued to argue that the Chiefs should bring the play back into their offensive arsenal.

The debate resurfaced against Denver during a crucial third-and-goal situation from the 1-yard line. With an open gap between center Creed Humphrey and right guard Trey Smith, Kansas City chose to hand the ball off to running back Kenneth Walker III, who was stopped by the Broncos’ defense.

After the game, Mahomes made it clear that he has no issue taking that type of risk if it helps the team win.

“I’m going to do whatever it takes to win. Quarterback sneak, whatever it is, it’s not like I’m scared to put my body on the line. That’s how I’ve played. It’s gotten me in trouble sometimes, and sometimes it’s helped the team. That’s stuff we’ll continue to evaluate and work on to make ourselves better for future references,” Mahomes said.

The decision was also questioned by former NFL player J.J. Watt , who believes the Chiefs will eventually need to bring the play back into their offense.

“You’ve gotta use the quarterback sneak at some point if you’re the Kansas City Chiefs. That was absolutely a false start,” Watt said.

Mahomes unlikely to challenge Andy Reid

Despite his willingness to run a QB sneak , Mahomes is unlikely to go against Andy Reid’s game plan. The relationship between the quarterback and head coach is one of the strongest in the NFL, and Mahomes has consistently shown complete trust in his coach’s decisions.

While Reid could give Mahomes more freedom in certain situations, the QB sneak appears to remain a limited option due to the history of his 2019 knee injury .

The Chiefs quarterback explained that if he does decide to use the play, he needs to be certain it will be successful.

“If I do that, it better work. I understand people watch the film and see stuff and want you to go out there and make it happen. But the play call is what we call, and we want to execute that play. That’s stuff that we evaluate and learn from. We’ll try to be better the next few weeks. If I call my own number, it’s got to work,” Mahomes said.

articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million mansion in Ohio is a nightmare: his neighbours are warning of a potential disaster
articles.standfirst: The Kansas City Chiefs star and Taylor Swift are facing objections from residents in Bratenahl
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs star and Taylor Swift are facing objections from residents in Bratenahl
articles.body:
T ravis Kelce 's return to his Ohio roots was supposed to provide a peaceful retreat, but turning his $5.35 million mansion into a more private home has proved far from straightforward.

The NFL star and his wife, Taylor Swift , purchased the historic property in Bratenahl, just outside Cleveland, and have since explored several changes to its exterior.

However, their plans have encountered resistance from neighbours who fear that some of the proposed improvements could create lasting problems for the surrounding community.

The most serious concern involves an ageing sewer pipe shared by the mansion and a neighbouring property.

Katherine Bolton , who has lived next door for more than three decades, warned that planting numerous evergreen trees close to the underground infrastructure could eventually cause substantial damage.

Speaking at a Bratenahl Architectural Review Board meeting, Bolton explained that the shared sewer line is approximately 115 years old. She believes the roots from the proposed planting could reach the pipe and create problems that would be expensive to resolve.

"When you plant that many trees from a short distance from a sewer line, you're going to have a problem in the future," Bolton said, according to Cleveland 19.

Her concerns extend beyond the possibility of damage to the existing pipe. Bolton said she had received an estimate of $75,000 to line the sewer against potential root intrusion, raising questions about who would be responsible for the expense if the infrastructure deteriorated.

She also warned that the consequences could be particularly difficult if the couple eventually sold the property, leaving the neighbouring homeowner to deal with any problems that emerged.

The possibility of sewage backups has therefore become a major sticking point in discussions about the landscaping.

Bolton has warned of potentially catastrophic consequences, although the likelihood and extent of any future damage have not been independently established.

The $7,500 repair has not ended the neighbours' concerns

Kelce and Swift's representatives have pointed to steps already taken to address some of the neighbourhood's complaints.

Property manager Patrick Hyland told the review board that the owners had paid $7,500 to repair a damaged section of the shared sewer line.

The team also arranged for the pipe to be jetted and cleaned, with the work presented as an effort to demonstrate that the couple wanted to maintain a positive relationship with nearby residents.

Their representatives have also made adjustments to the proposed security arrangements.

The original fencing proposal reportedly involved an eight-foot structure extending for approximately 1,190 feet. Following discussions with residents and officials, the design was reduced to six feet and moved two feet inside the property's boundary.

Two gates were also incorporated into the plans to preserve access to the sewer infrastructure. Another gate was added after neighbour Chuck Bauernschmidt raised concerns that the proposed arrangements would leave him feeling cut off.

However, the sewer dispute is not the only source of frustration.

Bauernschmidt , who has lived in Bratenahl for decades, objected to the removal of existing vegetation and questioned the potential impact of the new fencing on wildlife.

"I live here, been here for 47 years. I take offense when we start knocking trees down," he said during the discussions.

He also expressed concern about deer potentially becoming caught on pointed sections of the fence, adding to the list of issues surrounding the proposed changes.

Meanwhile, the landscaping plans have faced a separate regulatory obstacle. At the October 6 meeting, officials raised concerns that the proposed rear-yard trees could exceed the village's 10-foot height restriction.

The project's representatives acknowledged confusion over the requirements and indicated they were prepared to revise the design.

The board had already approved the front landscaping, but the rear-yard proposal remained unresolved. Officials scheduled another review for November 10, when a revised plan is expected to be considered.

For Kelce and Swift , the situation illustrates the challenges of balancing privacy and security with the expectations of an established residential community.

The mansion itself is an impressive property, reportedly measuring approximately 21,000 square feet, with eight bedrooms and 11 bathrooms. Its location overlooking Lake Erie and its historic character made it an attractive purchase for the couple.

But the renovation process has become a neighbourhood issue rather than simply a private home improvement project. Until the remaining landscaping questions are settled, the couple's plans for their Ohio retreat will continue to face scrutiny.

The $7,500 sewer repair represents a significant effort to address one immediate problem, but it has not removed the concerns surrounding the proposed trees and the future of the shared pipe. The November 10 meeting could therefore prove important in determining whether a compromise can finally be reached.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill has a plan B if he doesn't return to the NFL after being ignored by the Chiefs
articles.standfirst: The free-agent wide receiver is still working towards a comeback after a devastating knee injury, but his interests away from football could provide another direction if his playing career comes to an end
articles.summary: The free-agent wide receiver is still working towards a comeback after a devastating knee injury, but his interests away from football could provide another direction if his playing career comes to an end
articles.body:
T yreek Hill is not ready to close the door on the NFL , but the former Miami Dolphins star is already developing interests that could help him build a life beyond professional football.

The 32-year-old wide receiver has spent more than a year dealing with the consequences of a serious knee injury, and his hopes of returning to the field have yet to become reality.

Although the Kansas City Chiefs have been linked with a possible reunion, no agreement has materialized, leaving Hill without a team as the 2026 season progresses.

That uncertainty has made his comments about life away from the sport particularly interesting.

During an interview with PEOPLE earlier this year, Hill revealed that he had been learning to DJ, obtained a car dealership licence and was considering returning to education.

Music has become one of his interests while recovering, and he has already performed in front of an audience.

Hill explained that the experience gave him satisfaction because of the reaction from the people listening: "It was crazy, man. A lot of people were happy…I feel like when I DJ, I want to make people happy. I feel like my music, I want to make people feel good. I want to make people feel like it's a vibe. You know what I'm saying? So I learned how to DJ."

The comments suggest that Hill enjoys entertaining people in a different environment from the football field. However, he has been careful not to describe music as his definite next career.

"It's just something that I'm doing in the pastime…I feel like I'm a guy who can do a lot, man. I love DJ'ing. I love cars, so I also got my car dealership license. I'm also trying to get back into school,” he said.

Hill also identified construction as another area he would like to explore, revealing that he has ambitions beyond the entertainment industry.

"I'm very huge into general construction," he shares, revealing, "So I want to go back to school for that. I got a lot of passions for a lot of things."

The Chiefs connection remains uncertain as Hill works towards a comeback

Hill's immediate priority, however, remains getting his body ready for another NFL opportunity.

His injury occurred during Miami's September 29, 2025, game against the New York Jets . He dislocated his knee and suffered multiple ligament injuries, including a torn ACL, bringing his season to an abrupt end. The Dolphins subsequently released him in February 2026, making him a free agent.

The recovery has been particularly demanding. In July, Hill explained that he was still struggling to regain strength in his injured leg after undergoing two operations: "My left leg is the one that I injured. I have no power in my left leg at all, so I'm trying to regain all the power back in my left leg. But it's one day at a time."

His rehabilitation has progressed since then. In October, his agent, Drew Rosenhaus , indicated that Hill was close to full recovery and was speaking with multiple NFL teams about a possible return. Rosenhaus nevertheless stressed that nothing was imminent.

Kansas City has emerged as a potential destination because Hill spent the first six seasons of his professional career with the franchise.

He helped the Chiefs win Super Bowl LIV and developed a productive partnership with quarterback Patrick Mahomes before being traded to Miami in 2022.

Reports in October suggested the Chiefs had explored the possibility of bringing him back, particularly after injuries affected their receiving options. However, interest has not translated into a contract, and Hill remains unsigned.

There are also questions about how quickly he could return to his previous level following such a significant injury. His explosive speed was central to his success, so teams will want reassurance that his physical recovery is sufficient before committing to him.

Hill's achievements give him a strong case for another opportunity. He is an eight-time Pro Bowler and five-time first-team All-Pro, and was among the league's most dangerous offensive players during his time in Kansas City and Miami.

For now, his future remains divided between two possibilities. He continues to pursue the chance to play again, while DJing, cars and construction offer alternative interests if football eventually becomes part of his past.

His comments do not suggest that he has decided to retire. Instead, they show that Hill is beginning to consider what else he could do with his life, even as he works towards another NFL comeback.

A lot of people were happy…I feel like when I DJ, I want to make people happy. I feel like my music, I want to make people feel good. I want to make people feel like it's a vibe. You know what I'm saying? So I learned how to DJ."
The comments suggest that Hill enjoys entertaining people in a different environment from the football field. However, he has been careful not to describe music as his definite next career.

"It's just something that I'm doing in the pastime…I feel like I'm a guy who can do a lot, man. I love DJ'ing. I love cars, so I also got my car dealership license. I'm also trying to get back into school,” he said.
Hill also identified construction as another area he would like to explore, revealing that he has ambitions beyond the entertainment industry.
"I'm very huge into general construction," he shares, revealing, "So I want to go back to school for that. I got a lot of passions for a lot of things."
The Chiefs connection remains uncertain as Hill works towards a comeback
Hill's immediate priority, however, remains getting his body ready for another NFL opportunity.

His injury occurred during Miami's September 29, 2025, game against the New York Jets . He dislocated his knee and suffered multiple ligament injuries, including a torn ACL, bringing his season to an abrupt end. The Dolphins subsequently released him in February 2026, making him a free agent.

The recovery has been particularly demanding. In July, Hill explained that he was still struggling to regain strength in his injured leg after undergoing two operations: "My left leg is the one that I injured. I have no power in my left leg at all, so I'm trying to regain all the power back in my left leg. But it's one day at a time."

His rehabilitation has progressed since then. In October, his agent, Drew Rosenhaus , indicated that Hill was close to full recovery and was speaking with multiple NFL teams about a possible return. Rosenhaus nevertheless stressed that nothing was imminent.
Kansas City has emerged as a potential destination because Hill spent the first six seasons of his professional career with the franchise.
He helped the Chiefs win Super Bowl LIV and developed a productive partnership with quarterback Patrick Mahomes before being traded to Miami in 2022.

Reports in October suggested the Chiefs had explored the possibility of bringing him back, particularly after injuries affected their receiving options. However, interest has not translated into a contract, and Hill remains unsigned.

There are also questions about how quickly he could return to his previous level following such a significant injury. His explosive speed was central to his success, so teams will want reassurance that his physical recovery is sufficient before committing to him.

Hill's achievements give him a strong case for another opportunity. He is an eight-time Pro Bowler and five-time first-team All-Pro, and was among the league's most dangerous offensive players during his time in Kansas City and Miami.

For now, his future remains divided between two possibilities. He continues to pursue the chance to play again, while DJing, cars and construction offer alternative interests if football eventually becomes part of his past.
His comments do not suggest that he has decided to retire. Instead, they show that Hill is beginning to consider what else he could do with his life, even as he works towards another NFL comeback.

articles.title: Travis Kelce reveals Kylie's 'betrayal' after Jason's retirement still hurts: "My sister-in-law will tell me to my face, 'f**k you'"
articles.standfirst: Travis has learned that family ties don't always come before football loyalties
articles.summary: Travis has learned that family ties don't always come before football loyalties
articles.body:
Travis Kelce knows exactly where he stands with Kylie Kelce when the Kansas City Chiefs come up against the Philadelphia Eagles .

The Chiefs tight end might be part of her extended family, but that does not mean she is prepared to put her Philadelphia allegiance aside.

The subject resurfaced during the November 4 episode of the New Heights podcast, which Travis hosts alongside his older brother, Jason Kelce .

Discussing the Chiefs ' upcoming meeting with the New York Jets , the brothers were joined by producer Jake Chatzky , a longtime Jets supporter who found himself under pressure to declare which side he would back.

Chatzky initially attempted to avoid taking a position, telling Jason: “Don’t do this to me, Jason.”

He eventually admitted: “I’m absolutely rooting for Travis,” before adding, “For sure, I am 100 percent rooting for Travis.”

Travis wasn't entirely convinced by the declaration. He immediately joked: “Do you hear that Jets fans? He’s a f**king phony.”

The Chiefs star then added: “Don’t f**king lie to my face.”

However, the conversation gave Travis an opportunity to highlight the difference between Chatzky 's divided loyalties and Kylie's unwavering support for Philadelphia.

“My sister-in-law will tell me to my face, ‘F**k you,’” Travis joked. “I hope the Birds win.”

There is little doubt that Kylie is comfortable being honest about her football preferences, even when the person on the other side is someone she loves.

The apparent family 'betrayal' is more of a running joke than a genuine source of tension, with Travis seemingly appreciating that she never pretends to support the Chiefs .

Kylie Kelce has never hidden Eagles allegiance

Kylie 's connection to Philadelphia goes well beyond her marriage to Jason . The Pennsylvania native has maintained close relationships with the Eagles organization and the local community, while her husband spent 13 seasons representing the franchise before announcing his retirement in March 2024.

That history helps explain why she has never been willing to abandon the team, even when the Chiefs are involved. Her position became particularly relevant ahead of Super Bowl LIX in February 2025, when Kansas City faced Philadelphia.

Kylie made a point of publicly supporting Travis , acknowledging the work he had put into his career and explaining that she would always celebrate his achievements.

“I think that Travis has been there for his entire career, he has worked so hard and put in so much time that I am truly, as always, cheering Travis on,” she said on her podcast. “And I love him, he's my family. So, I will always cheer on Travis' accomplishments and hopefully successes.”

However, she was equally clear about where her sporting identity remained.

“I was raised to bleed green,” Kylie explained, pointing to her friendships and continuing connections within the Eagles organization.

The Super Bowl ultimately went Philadelphia's way, with the Eagles securing a convincing 40-22 victory over the Chiefs .

For Jason , who had retired from the Eagles the previous year, the result created an uncomfortable emotional situation as he watched his former team defeat his younger brother.

Jason later discussed the difficulty of balancing those loyalties on New Heights, admitting that watching the game was more uncomfortable than he had anticipated.

The family dynamic has therefore produced some memorable football moments, but Kylie has consistently maintained that supporting Travis personally does not require her to change teams.

With Jason now retired and Travis continuing his NFL career in Kansas City, the rivalry remains an entertaining feature of their family life. And judging by Travis ' latest comments, he would much rather receive Kylie's honest response than expect her to pretend the Eagles are not her first choice.

articles.title: Andy Reid's latest decision regarding Harrison Butker reveals serious doubts about Justin Tucker
articles.standfirst: The Chiefs kicking situation has taken another twist following consecutive defeats
articles.summary: The Chiefs kicking situation has taken another twist following consecutive defeats
articles.body:
J ustin Tucker 's arrival in Kansas City appeared to place Harrison Butker 's future under immediate threat, but Andy Reid has made it clear that the former Baltimore Ravens star will have to wait longer for his opportunity.

The Chiefs coach confirmed Wednesday that Butker will remain the team's starting kicker against the New York Jets , despite another expensive mistake contributing to Kansas City's 28-24 defeat against the Denver Broncos .

The decision comes only a week after Kansas City signed Tucker to its practice squad, a move that appeared to signal growing frustration with Butke r's inability to rediscover the consistency that helped the franchise win three Super Bowls.

However, Reid has resisted making an immediate change, even with the Chiefs attempting to recover from consecutive defeats and their special teams becoming an increasingly significant concern.

"Harrison will be up, yeah," Reid told reporters Wednesday when asked whether Butker would handle kicking duties against the Jets.

The confirmation leaves Tucker facing further uncertainty about his NFL comeback, although Reid hasn't publicly suggested that concerns over the veteran's ability are preventing his promotion.

Butker receives another chance

Butker 's latest setback came during the fourth quarter against Denver, when he missed a 54-yard field goal that could have substantially improved Kansas City's chances of securing victory.

The Chiefs had entered the final quarter leading 24-13, but Denver scored twice to overturn the deficit while Butker failed to convert an opportunity that would have changed the team's late-game requirements.

The 31-year-old has now converted just 12 of 18 field goal attempts this season, leaving him with a success rate of 66.7 percent through seven appearances.

His struggles extend beyond the current campaign, with 16 unsuccessful kicks since the beginning of last season, the highest total recorded by any NFL player during that period.

Butker acknowledged his responsibility after the Broncos defeat, offering a particularly blunt assessment of his latest mistake.

"Just missed it. Didn't even give it a chance," Butker said. "When I say bad miss, like, just completely missed the ball. Didn't even give it a chance. Didn't feel good off the foot. Just not good."

Reid subsequently suggested that Denver's aggressive blocking formation had influenced Butker 's approach, contributing to the ball drifting wide of the uprights.

Tucker's controversial Chiefs return on hold

Tucker joined Kansas City's practice squad in late October after the Chiefs evaluated several kickers, including former Los Angeles Rams player Harrison Mevis .

The 36-year-old spent 13 seasons with Baltimore, establishing himself among the most accurate kickers in NFL history before his release in May 2025.

However, his departure followed allegations of sexual misconduct involving massage therapists, which Tucker denied. The NFL subsequently imposed a 10-game suspension for violating its personal conduct policy.

His arrival in Kansas City attracted considerable criticism, but the Chiefs nevertheless viewed him as an experienced option amid Butker 's declining accuracy.

Despite his own struggles, Butker has spoken positively about his new teammate and acknowledged that the competition has created additional pressure.

"Justin's been great. Enjoyed talking with him and getting to know him a little bit more," Butker said after Sunday's defeat. "So it was a good week of practice, but doesn't matter, you've got to make them in the game."

Reid 's decision gives Butker another opportunity against the Jets , but the continued presence of Tucker ensures the competition is unlikely to disappear while Kansas City's kicking problems persist.

articles.title: Tom Brady ‘shuts down’ complaints from Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes: “I hate pouring salt in the wound, but the knee flinched”
articles.standfirst: The seven-time Super Bowl champion explained why Kansas City cannot blame officials for defeat
articles.summary: The seven-time Super Bowl champion explained why Kansas City cannot blame officials for defeat
articles.body:
Tom Brady believes the Kansas City Chiefs have more pressing problems than a disputed officiating decision, delivering a firm response to the controversy surrounding their dramatic defeat against the Denver Broncos .

Kansas City suffered a 28-24 loss on Sunday after surrendering an 11-point fourth-quarter lead, but the most contentious moment arrived with just four seconds remaining when Patrick Mahomes appeared to find Rashee Rice for the winning touchdown.

The celebration was short-lived, however, as officials penalized right tackle Jaylon Moore for a false start, wiping out the score and forcing Kansas City to attempt another play from six yards out.

Mahomes was subsequently sacked by Denver's Malcolm Roach , completing a frustrating afternoon that left the Chiefs with consecutive defeats after opening the season with five straight victories.

Head coach Andy Reid questioned the penalty afterward, while Mahomes expressed frustration about such a marginal infringement being called during the decisive moments of a game.

Brady , however, reviewed the incident and reached a different conclusion, suggesting Kansas City's frustration was misplaced.

The former New England Patriots quarterback addressed the incident during his latest FOX Sports power rankings, where Kansas City's defeat contributed to another drop in the standings.

Brady acknowledged the disappointment surrounding the result but insisted officials had correctly identified Moore 's movement before the snap.

"I hate pouring salt in the wound, but the knee flinched. The refs made the right call," Brady said.

His assessment contrasted with Reid 's explanation during his postgame press conference, when the Chiefs coach maintained that he had not witnessed a clear infringement.

"I didn't see it," Reid said. "That's one man's opinion. I saw him move his head, but I didn't see a false start."

Mahomes also questioned the timing of the decision while accepting that his team ultimately had to live with the officials' ruling.

"But a lot of times in those big moments, the little stuff doesn't get called like that," Mahomes told reporters.

The Chiefs committed 11 penalties for 105 yards against Denver, with those mistakes contributing to their inability to protect a commanding fourth-quarter advantage.

Brady identifies encouraging sign

Although Brady supported the officials, he was considerably more positive about Mahomes ' performance, suggesting the quarterback had rediscovered his usual effectiveness.

Mahomes threw for 321 yards and three touchdowns without an interception, producing a significant improvement after struggling to generate passing touchdowns in recent games.

Brady placed Kansas City ninth in his latest rankings after previously having the Chiefs second, reflecting the consequences of consecutive road defeats against Seattle and Denver.

The loss also allowed the Broncos to move ahead in the AFC West standings, increasing the importance of Kansas City's upcoming home game against the New York Jets .

Despite the setback, Brady believes Mahomes ' improved form offers encouragement if the Chiefs can eliminate the penalties that have undermined their recent performances.

His verdict leaves Kansas City with a straightforward challenge which is to focus less on the disputed decision and more on correcting the mistakes that allowed Denver to complete its comeback.

articles.title: Damien Williams claims Chiefs were “cheated” by the referees as Kansas City loses control of AFC West
articles.standfirst: A disputed late penalty has sparked criticism from the former Super Bowl champion
articles.summary: A disputed late penalty has sparked criticism from the former Super Bowl champion
articles.body:
Damien Williams believes the Kansas City Chiefs were robbed of a crucial victory against the Denver Broncos , with the former Super Bowl-winning running back suggesting that questionable officiating played a decisive role in his old team's latest defeat.

Kansas City surrendered an 11-point fourth-quarter advantage at Empower Field at Mile High on Sunday, eventually losing 28-24 in a result that allowed Denver to overtake the Chiefs at the top of the AFC West.

However, the most controversial moment arrived in the closing seconds, when Patrick Mahomes appeared to complete a remarkable comeback by finding Rashee Rice for a touchdown from Denver's one-yard line.

Officials instead penalized offensive tackle Jaylon Moore for a false start, wiping out the score before Mahomes was sacked on the final play.

The decision left Kansas City facing consecutive defeats after beginning the season with five straight victories, although Williams believes there were encouraging signs despite the disappointing outcome.

Speaking on The Damien Williams Show, the former Kansas City running back made clear that he was not convinced his old team deserved to lose.

"For me personally, like I said, I took a lot of positivity out of that game, and I'm just ready to keep rolling to see what they've got coming for us," Williams said.

"Because like I said, we lost. I do not feel like we lost. I feel like we got bamboozled, but that's neither here nor there. Referees, but hey, it was a tough one, though."

His frustration echoed concerns raised by Chiefs coach Andy Reid , who questioned the false start decision after the game.

"I didn't see it," Reid told reporters. "That's one man's opinion. I saw him move his head, but I didn't see a false start."

However, replays showed movement from Moore before the snap, making the officials' decision defensible under NFL rules despite disagreement over its severity.

The penalty moved Kansas City back five yards, allowing Denver's pass rush to pressure Mahomes before Malcolm Roach completed the game-ending sack.

Chiefs face bigger problem after losing AFC West lead

The disputed decision was only part of a difficult afternoon for Kansas City, which committed 11 penalties for 105 yards during the divisional contest.

Mahomes threw for 321 yards and three touchdowns, but the Chiefs failed to score in the fourth quarter after entering the final period with a 24-13 advantage.

Harrison Butker also missed a 54-yard field goal, giving Denver another opportunity to complete its comeback.

Broncos quarterback Bo Nix helped engineer the turnaround, with rookie running back Jonah Coleman eventually scoring the touchdown that put Denver ahead.

The victory improved the Broncos ' record to 6-2, while Kansas City slipped to 5-2, surrendering first place in the division midway through the regular season.

Williams remains encouraged by the Chiefs ' performance, but the defeat has placed renewed emphasis on discipline and late-game execution.

Kansas City will attempt to respond against the New York Jets at Arrowhead Stadium, where another defeat would deepen concerns about its suddenly vulnerable position in the AFC West.

articles.title: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice files for bankruptcy amid $3.45 million debt crisis
articles.standfirst: Rashee Rice’s off-field troubles continue as the Chiefs wide receiver files for bankruptcy, revealing millions in debt while Kansas City searches for offensive help.
articles.summary: Rashee Rice’s off-field troubles continue as the Chiefs wide receiver files for bankruptcy, revealing millions in debt while Kansas City searches for offensive help.
articles.body:
In an unexpected turn, Kansas City Chiefs star wide receiver Rashee Rice filed for bankruptcy on Wednesday in federal court, adding another complication to the difficult legal situation he faces as the franchise reaches the midpoint of the season.

According to reports from ESPN journalists Nate Taylor and Michael Rothstein , Rice submitted the filing in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the N orthern District of Texas , where he disclosed more than $3.45 million in debts .

According to the documents filed by the player, more than $2.1 million of that amount relates to civil lawsuits against him. Some of these claims have already been resolved through financial settlements, while others remain pending judicial resolution.

The receiver faces multiple lawsuits connected to the high-speed multi-vehicle accident that occurred in Dallas in 2024 . In addition, his ex-partner has accused him of alleged assaults during the two years they were in a relationship.

As a result of his involvement in the accident, Rice received a six-game suspension from the NFL and returned to action with the Chiefs during the 2025 season .

Rashee Rice reveals his financial problems

Although Rice is projected to earn more than $1.5 million in base salary during the 2026 season , the bankruptcy documents paint a complicated financial picture.

The receiver reported having only $13,640 in personal bank accounts, along with $677,054 in assets, of which $421,825 corresponds to deferred compensation, according to ESPN .

The filing also notes that his largest creditor is claiming a debt of $979,837 related to one of the settlements reached after the car accident.

In addition, Rice is disputing some of the amounts claimed against him, including nearly $900,000 stemming from lawsuits filed by both accident victims and his ex-partner.

The player requested protection under Chapter 7 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code, a process designed for individuals who cannot meet their financial obligations and that allows certain non-exempt assets to be liquidated to pay creditors.

The court documents state that $39,241 of his assets were classified as non-exempt and could therefore be used in the process.

Chiefs looking for solutions at wide receiver

While Rice deals with his off-field issues, the Chiefs continue evaluating options to strengthen their wide receiver group before the trade deadline.

Injuries have hit Kansas City hard, with Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy , and Tyquan Thornton either out of rhythm or limited, and none of them have maintained consistent production when available.

The situation has not improved with young players Jalen Royals and Cyrus Allen, who have yet to take the expected step forward in the offense.

Facing a lack of depth, Kansas City could look to add a receiver before the trade deadline. Among the names mentioned as potential targets are Josh Downs (Colts), Brian Thomas Jr. (Jaguars), Dontayvion Wicks (Eagles), Quentin Johnston (Chargers), Calvin Ridley (Titans), Chris Godwin (Buccaneers), and Jerry Jeudy (Browns).

With their sights set on another Super Bowl run, the Chiefs need to regain offensive consistency. Rice remains a key piece in Patrick Mahomes ’ attack, but the franchise may be forced to seek outside help to compensate for the problems that have affected its receiver group.

In addition, Rice is disputing some of the amounts claimed against him, including nearly $900,000 stemming from lawsuits filed by both accident victims and his ex-partner.

The player requested protection under Chapter 7 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code, a process designed for individuals who cannot meet their financial obligations and that allows certain non-exempt assets to be liquidated to pay creditors.
The court documents state that $39,241 of his assets were classified as non-exempt and could therefore be used in the process.
Chiefs looking for solutions at wide receiver
While Rice deals with his off-field issues, the Chiefs continue evaluating options to strengthen their wide receiver group before the trade deadline.
Injuries have hit Kansas City hard, with Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy , and Tyquan Thornton either out of rhythm or limited, and none of them have maintained consistent production when available.
The situation has not improved with young players Jalen Royals and Cyrus Allen, who have yet to take the expected step forward in the offense.

Facing a lack of depth, Kansas City could look to add a receiver before the trade deadline. Among the names mentioned as potential targets are Josh Downs (Colts), Brian Thomas Jr. (Jaguars), Dontayvion Wicks (Eagles), Quentin Johnston (Chargers), Calvin Ridley (Titans), Chris Godwin (Buccaneers), and Jerry Jeudy (Browns).

With their sights set on another Super Bowl run, the Chiefs need to regain offensive consistency. Rice remains a key piece in Patrick Mahomes ’ attack, but the franchise may be forced to seek outside help to compensate for the problems that have affected its receiver group.

articles.title: Donna Kelce raking it in! Taylor Swift's mother-in-law sells her Florida condo for huge profit
articles.standfirst: A property improvement project that became a running joke for Travis and Jason Kelce has ended with a lucrative sale
articles.summary: A property improvement project that became a running joke for Travis and Jason Kelce has ended with a lucrative sale
articles.body:
Donna Kelce 's decision to renovate her Florida home has ended with a substantial financial gain, as the mother of two NFL stars has reportedly sold the property for considerably more than its original purchase price.

The 74-year-old, whose family has become increasingly prominent through her son Travis Kelce 's marriage to Taylor Swift , recently completed the sale of her Orlando condominium for $485,000, according to property records obtained by TMZ.

Donna purchased the two-bedroom property for $355,000 in 2019, meaning its value increased by $130,000 during her ownership, although renovation expenses and transaction costs would reduce any actual profit.

The sale follows a home improvement project earlier this year that unexpectedly became an internet sensation after news emerged that she was replacing several windows and doors.

What began as a routine renovation quickly attracted widespread attention, with Travis and his older brother Jason turning the publicity into a running family joke.

Now, months after the unlikely controversy, Donna has reportedly exchanged her condominium for a larger lakefront residence elsewhere in Orlando.

The property, measuring approximately 1,434 square feet, contains two bedrooms and two bathrooms and had served as Donna 's Florida residence for several years.

Earlier in 2026, she arranged improvements involving nine windows and six doors, with the work becoming public through property records and subsequent media coverage.

The attention amused her sons, particularly Travis , who joked that his mother had not approached him for assistance despite the scale of the reported improvements.

"If she needed a guy to come screw some door hinges in, she could have just called me," the Chiefs tight end said during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show. "But I guess she's doing a big massive renovate."

Jason also joined the jokes, posting a mock breaking-news announcement about his own ordinary activities after seeing the attention surrounding his mother's property.

"BREAKING!! Sources confirm Donna Kelce's eldest son watched 2 hours of Bluey yesterday," the retired Philadelphia Eagles center wrote on X.

Donna later appeared on the brothers' New Heights podcast, explaining that the improvements were far less dramatic than some reports suggested.

She described the attention as "so stupid," while clarifying that the work was intended to address outdated windows that struggled with Florida's changing temperatures.

Donna Kelce moves into bigger Orlando home

The conclusion of Donna 's property sale has also revealed that she's apparently remaining in Florida rather than relocating closer to either of her famous sons.

According to the transaction paperwork cited by TMZ, her new address is a three-bedroom, two-bathroom lakefront home measuring approximately 2,549 square feet.

That represents an increase of more than 1,100 square feet compared with her previous residence, offering considerably more space in a different setting.

The move comes during another eventful period for the Kelce family, with Travis continuing his NFL career and Jason maintaining a prominent media presence following retirement.

Donna has also developed her own public profile through television appearances, advertising partnerships and her regular presence at major sporting events.

Her latest real estate transaction adds another chapter to that growing attention, turning an ordinary family renovation story into a financial success that has once again placed her in the headlines.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes gets new receiver Bub Means for the Chiefs but can he deliver what Tyreek Hill once did?
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs have added a new wide receiver, but Bub Means arrives with a much bigger question attached: Can he give the quarterback the kind of impact Tyreek Hill once brought to Kansas City? The Chiefs signed Means to their practice squad Thursday, Nov. 5, after he worked out for the team. The move gives Kansas City another option as it looks for depth at receiver.
articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs have added a new wide receiver, but Bub Means arrives with a much bigger question attached: Can he give the quarterback the kind of impact Tyreek Hill once brought to Kansas City? The Chiefs signed Means to their practice squad Thursday, Nov. 5, after he worked out for the team. The move gives Kansas City another option as it looks for depth at receiver.

The timing follows a difficult stretch for the Chiefs. They have lost two straight games, including a 28-24 defeat to the Denver Broncos in Week 8, but remain 5-2 after seven games. Mahomes has thrown for 1,795 yards and 12 touchdowns, with four interceptions. Kansas City hosts the New York Jets on Sunday, Nov. 8, at noon CT.

Bub Means has a long way to go to match Tyreek Hill

Bub Means has shown flashes, but his NFL résumé is still limited. The New Orleans Saints drafted him in the fifth round in 2024, and he caught nine passes for 118 yards and a touchdown in seven games as a rookie.

An ankle injury kept him out for the 2025 season. After stints with New Orleans and Cleveland, he is now joining Kansas City’s practice squad.

His college production offers a reason for the Chiefs to take a closer look . At Pittsburgh in 2023, Means caught 41 passes for 721 yards and six touchdowns, averaging 17.6 yards per catch.

That big-play potential could make him an intriguing developmental option, but his college numbers have yet to translate into sustained NFL production.

Tyreek Hill set a far higher bar during his six seasons with Kansas City, recording 479 catches, 6,630 receiving yards and 56 receiving touchdowns. He became one of Mahomes’ most dangerous targets, able to turn a short completion into a game-changing play.

Means has only 118 career receiving yards, so the comparison is more a measure of what Kansas City needs than an expectation he can immediately fill Hill’s role.

For now, Bub is a practice-squad addition, not a guaranteed answer to the Chiefs’ receiving questions. He will need to earn opportunities and show that his speed and playmaking can carry over at the NFL level.

Kansas City Chiefs may be hoping to uncover another useful target for Patrick Mahomes; matching what Tyreek Hill once delivered is a much taller challenge.

articles.title: Brittany Mahomes gives fans a sweet look at family life with Patrick and their three kids
articles.standfirst: The quarterback has stated that he wants his children to have the freedom to develop their own interests
articles.summary: The quarterback has stated that he wants his children to have the freedom to develop their own interests
articles.body:
P atrick Mahomes may be one of the biggest stars in the NFL, but his most enthusiastic supporters are not necessarily sitting in the stands. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback had his family cheering him on during the team’s recent matchup against the Denver Broncos, with wife Brittany Mahomes and their three young children showing their support in unmistakable Chiefs red.

Brittany offered fans a glimpse of the family’s game-day experience on Thursday, Nov. 5, sharing a collection of photographs and videos from the Nov. 1 game at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver. The images captured a heartwarming side of the Mahomes family, with Brittany and the children enjoying time together on the sidelines while supporting Patrick during his 10th NFL season.

There was just one small complication before kickoff: getting three children under the age of five ready for a football game. “If you saw our wrestling match pre-game…no ya didn’t,” Brittany joked in her Instagram caption, adding a laughing emoji. The comment offered a humorous glimpse into the challenges of bringing three young children to an NFL game, even when their father happens to be one of the league’s biggest stars.

The Mahomes children steal the spotlight in Chiefs red

The photo carousel began with Brittany sitting on the sidelines wearing a Chiefs-red top, smiling alongside son Bronze, 3, and daughter Golden , 21 months. Both children were dressed in colors representing their father’s team. Another photograph gave Golden a moment of her own on the field, while Bronze enjoyed some time cuddling with his mother.

The sweetest images, however, came when all three siblings gathered around Brittany for family photographs. The children could also be seen playing with their game passes, laughing, hugging and piling on top of one another as they enjoyed the atmosphere.

The family eventually reunited with Patrick during a break in the action, giving the quarterback an opportunity to spend a few moments with his biggest supporters. Videos shared by Brittany also showed her encouraging Golden to cheer for her father, adding another memorable moment to the family’s game-day collection.

The Chiefs ultimately lost the matchup 28-24 against Denver, but the result did little to diminish the enthusiasm surrounding the Mahomes family’s appearance.

Patrick Mahomes wants his children to find their own passions

Patrick and Brittany, both 31, have been together since their high school days and married in 2022. They are parents to daughters Sterling, 5, and Golden , 21 months, and son Bronze, 3. While football is obviously a major part of their family life, Patrick has previously explained that he wants his children to have the freedom to develop their own interests rather than feel obligated to follow in his footsteps.

During an October 2022 episode of Football in America, before Golden was born, the three-time Super Bowl MVP discussed how he planned to introduce his children to sports. “I’m going to teach my son, my daughter all the fundamentals and whatever they want to learn,” Mahomes said. However, he emphasized that he would not pressure them into pursuing football or any particular activity.

“But at the same time ... I want to let it be about them,” he explained. Mahomes also credited his own parents for allowing him to explore his interests without imposing expectations.

That philosophy appears to be reflected in the family’s approach to raising their children, allowing them to enjoy football games and other experiences without making their father’s profession the center of their childhood.
